fixes.why: 0.034 ms is 34 microseconds, so the printed 0.34 microseconds was out by a factor of 100 [bprv-15]. The operation count is left at 10,737,418,240: under the problem's own counting rule (one multiply and one add = two operations, from B's kv-cache lesson) that is already 2 x the 5,368,709,120 cached numbers, so the doubling the packet proposed is not applied. 4096^2 = 16,777,216, so 16.8 million scores per head; 67 million is 8192^2 [bprv-15]. The count is never used by the following arithmetic, so the 141 ms answer stands.

indexPrompt.eff-cut-after-degree-six: The softmax weight is a dot product of two endless lists, because the series for e to a power turns one dot product into a sum of dot products of longer lists. Compute the dot product of the two lists cut after degree 6, count how many numbers a cut after degree 3 needs at a head size of 64, and explain what can go wrong when a cut ends after an odd degree.
indexPrompt.eff-how-long-a-session-takes: An 80-layer model with 64 heads of 128 two-byte numbers is served on an accelerator that does 312 trillion operations and reads 2 trillion bytes a second. A request has a 4,096-token prompt read in one prefill run and a 200-token reply written one decode run at a time, with a multiply and an add counted as two operations. Time one decode run, time the prefill, then say which phase costs more and what grouped-query attention with 8 groups does to that balance.
indexPrompt.eff-the-state-after-the-next-token: A linear attention head has just read "the cat sat" and writes "on", and the new token joins the running state of six numbers before its own output is read. Give the updated total of key numbers, the head's output, and the weight linear attention gives the oldest key.
